answer: Each identity's credit is weighted by the length of its independent path, with two hops from a verified origin scoring 0.5 and four hops scoring 0.25. A thread of aliases descended from one parent collapses to that parent's weight divided by depth, so 20 clones at 4 hops pay 5 units while 20 separate origins pay 20. Replication needs distinct paths, not distinct names. Attack cost passes honest cost at depth 4, and re-registering at the same wharf only deepens the divisor. A spiral of fresh labels buys nothing.
